newsitem.title: USA: Rep. Largent suggests Gingrich steps aside.
newsitem.headline: Rep. Largent suggests Gingrich steps aside.

text.p: Republican Congressman Steve Largent said on Sunday he supported suggestions that Republican House Speaker Newt Gingrich step aside temporarily while he resolves ethics charges against him.

Largent of Oklahoma said during a television interview that he would be in favour of Republican Representative Henry Hyde, of Illinois, taking over as Speaker of the House while Gingrich dealt with the ethics charges.
He also said he thought there was some support among other House Republicans for such a move.

Asked during the Fox News Sunday programme about the possibility of Gingrich stepping aside, Largent said: "I think it's a good idea and I think it would reduce the amount of rhetoric that you would hear on the floor of Congress and allow us to work more constructively and move forward."

Largent, asked if he thought there was a lot of support for such a move among House Republicans, said: "I think that behind closed doors there would be, but publicly people would be fearful to say that on national TV."
Largent was elected to the House in 1994, the same year Gingrich was elected Speaker.
The Ethics Committee is investigating Democrat charges that Gingrich's tax-exempt foundation funnelled money illegally to Republican candidates in the 1994 Congressional elections.
In September the Ethics Committee dismissed three charges against Gingrich, but at least four more remained unresolved.
